patch.objective: Recognize scene hazards -- traffic, fire, electricity, hazardous materials, violence, unstable structures -- and decide whether the scene is safe to enter
secondaryObjectives: Protect the patient, bystanders and crew at a traffic incident
Decide which additional resources to request early -- ALS, fire, law enforcement, hazmat, air medical -- and justify the request
Communicate a concise, organized handoff report to the receiving clinician

sources.cite: National Registry of EMTs. EMT examination test plan
sources.note: Relayed from the course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/ems.ts and labs/ems-sources.ts, read in NREMT's own documents 2026-11-09); not re-read for this case. Scene Size-up and Safety: recognize hazards and decide whether the scene is safe to enter; request resources.

sources.cite: Electrical Safety Foundation International (ESFI). Downed Power Line Safety: Always Assume Downed Lines are Live (published 2019-03-27, modified 2025-02-20)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: 'Downed power lines can energize the ground up to 35 feet away'; 'Warn others to stay at least 35 feet away'; 'ALWAYS assume a downed power line is live and avoid going near it or anything in contact with it'; in a vehicle: 'Stay in place or inside your vehicle unless you see fire or smoke'; if you must leave, 'Do not touch the ground and vehicle at the same time', 'Jump from the vehicle with your feet together', 'Shuffle away'.

sources.cite: NASEMSO. National Model EMS Clinical Guidelines, Version 3.0 (March 2022): Electrical Injuries
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the full text Iowa HHS hosts (https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/198/download) through summarizing fetches with quotes; NASEMSO's own page, read the same day, still presents Version 3 (2022) as current and names no later version. 'Verify scene is secure. The electrical source must be disabled prior to assessment'; shut off electrical power; continuous cardiac monitoring and a 12-lead as soon as feasible; a burn center whenever possible. The section does not cover downed lines (see the ESFI source).

sources.cite: NHTSA. National EMS Scope of Practice Model 2019: Including Change Notices 1.0 and 2.0 (DOT HS 813 151, 2021-08-01)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17: the record page (title, report number, date; the change notices add intramuscular injection, vaccination in a public health emergency and nasal swab collection at EMT and above) and the PDF's skill tables through a summarizing fetch whose table columns were partly unclear, so placement was checked against the course's own reading (backend/supabase/seed/labs/ems-sources.ts, 2026-11-09) and REQ-241's reading (2026-11-11). EMR: oxygen, BVM, naloxone (intranasal or auto-injector), unit-dose hazmat antidote auto-injectors, tourniquet, wound packing, emergency moves, manual stabilization; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, oral glucose, aspirin, the patient's own nitroglycerin, an inhaled bronchodilator, CPAP, the epinephrine auto-injector. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways, waveform capnography, sublingual nitroglycerin and a limited list of IV and IM drugs (dextrose, naloxone). Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing, needle chest decompression, intubation and medicated infusions. No newer model was found on 2026-11-17.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

brief.situation: 21:10. You are an EMT on the first-arriving fire engine, first on scene: a car has hit a utility pole on a dark two-lane road. A downed line lies across the hood. The driver, a man in his 30s, is in his seat with a bleeding forehead. A few people from nearby houses are gathering.
handover: Your dispatcher can reach the power company and law enforcement. The transporting ambulance is on the way, about 15 minutes out.
Within EMT scope: scene safety, bleeding control, assessment and handover to the transporting crew. You cannot make a line safe; only the utility can.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
Every assessment and treatment takes the time it would on a real call. Scene time and the drive run on the clock.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends when care is handed over, then a debrief scores what you did.
